articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr.'s Limited Giants Role Addressed by Giants OC, WR Has 0 Targets Through 2 Games
articles.summary: Odell Beckham Jr.'s reunion with the New York Giants has been quiet so far, as the receiver has received no targets through the first two games.
articles.body:
Odell Beckham Jr.'s reunion with the New York Giants has been quiet so far, as the receiver has received no targets through the first two games.

Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy addressed the slow start for Beckham on Thursday.

"We're trying to slowly package him into things offensively," Nagy said. "So it's not that he's just a backup. There's some times that, whatever it is, personnel-wise, we have it on the game plan; we just didn't get to it... We're one injury away from him being in all the time."

Underperforming Players With the Most to Prove 🏈

While the Giants didn't bring Beckham in to be one of their top targets on offense, it is a bit surprising to see how little he's been used through the first two games. During Monday's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, he played just three snaps in the entire game, despite Malik Nabers having to sit out some because of a shoulder injury.

New York hasn't managed to get its offense going much through the first two games, with tight end Isaiah Likely leading the way with 111 receiving yards and two touchdowns. He leads the team in both receptions and targets.

The Giants will face the Tennessee Titans this week, and perhaps going up against a lesser opponent will give them the chance to experiment with Beckham a bit more.

New York will need to find something to get the offense going with starting quarterback Jaxson Dart out for the year.

Beckham spent his first five NFL seasons with New York before stops with the Cleveland Browns, Los Angeles Rams, Baltimore Ravens and Miami Dolphins. He's far from the receiver he once was, though the Giants clearly felt like he was serviceable enough to sign him to the 53-man roster.

The 33-year-old is looking to have a memorable reunion with the Giants, but he'll first have to find his way into the regular rotation.

articles.title: 49ers’ Kyle Juszczyk fined nearly $15K after NFL says he pretended to chug beer on field
articles.summary: The NFL fined San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk for an alleged act of “offensive demonstration” — when the league says he feigned chugging a brew in the end zone to celebrate a touchdown.
articles.body: The NFL fined San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk for an alleged act of “offensive demonstration” — when the league says he feigned chugging a brew in the end zone to celebrate a touchdown. In the third quarter of an eventual 35-13 Niners win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, Juszczyk caught a 6-yard scoring toss from Brock Purdy. Juszczyk embraced teammates Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel before bringing his right hand up to his mouth. Juszczyk tilted his head back, then mimed drinking a pretend liquid. That celly was deemed to be excessive and unsportsmanlike, leading to a fine of nearly $15,000, ESPN first reported on Thursday. “Your imitation of chugging a beer constituted an offensive demonstration and could reasonably be construed as being in poor taste,” the NFL wrote in its fine letter, according to ESPN. Juszczyk then confirmed the report with a bemused re-post on X: “Can’t make this stuff up.” The 35-year-old Juszczyk is in his 14th year of pro football and 10th with the Niners. He’s one of team’s most popular players, with 49ers faithful breaking out into chants of “Juice,” his nickname, every time the Harvard graduate carries or catches the ball. The 10-time Pro Bowl fullback has also gained fame in recent years through the rising profile of his wife, designer Kristin Juszczyk. The football fashionista has a line with the NFL. NFL fines are typically disclosed publicly on Saturdays and representatives for the league could not be immediately reached for comment on Thursday. A representative for the 49ers said fines are a league-player issue so the Niners have “no involvement or awareness in that process.”

articles.title: NFL fines player nicknamed 'Juice' $14,926 for using a drinking celebration, calling it offensive
articles.summary: Kyle Juszczyk is appealing a $14,926 NFL fine for his 'drinking' TD celebration against the Dolphins, which the league called an offensive demonstration.
articles.body: The NFL, which has an official beer sponsor, an official drink sponsor, and allows clubs to sell and serve alcoholic beverages in its stadiums during games, has fined San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk for using a play celebration that imitates him "chugging a beer." Let this marinate for a moment. It gets crazier. TEXANS' AZEEZ AL-SHAAIR TO BE FINED ONCE AGAIN BY NFL FOR WEARING PRO-PALESTINIAN PERSONAL MESSAGE ON EYEBLACK Juszczyk received a letter from the league this week informing him he is being fined $14,926 for celebrating a touchdown by giving the universal symbol of taking a drink. The league told Juszczyk he violated Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, when he did an "imitation of chugging a beer" after scoring a touchdown at the 5:46 mark of the third quarter against the Miami Dolphins. NFL RESTARTS SOCIAL JUSTICE MESSAGING WHILE BATTLING DOMESTIC ABUSE, DRUNK DRIVING AND PROSTITUTION ARRESTS "Your imitation of chugging a beer constituted an offensive demonstration and could reasonably be construed as being in poor taste," the league's fine letter to Juszczyk reads in part. The letter also said, "players are expected to conduct themselves in a manner that reflects positively on the game and is consistent with NFL standards of sportsmanship." NFL FINES SAINTS AND COWBOYS $500K FOR PRACTICE BRAWL, BUT FIGHTS WON'T STOP UNLESS PLAYERS GET FINED Further offenses, Juszczyk was warned, would result in an escalation of disciplinary action, up to and including suspension. Juszcyzk is appealing the fine, per a source. Juszczyk scored his touchdown against the Dolphins, celebrated, and soon afterward the television broadcast cut to a Michelob Ultra beer commercial. Not. Making. This. Up. The NFL has an official beer. Anheuser-Busch and its major brand, Bud Light, serve as the official beer and hard seltzer sponsor of the NFL under an agreement running through the 2026-27 season. And as part of that deal, the beer has promotional agreements with more than two dozen current NFL players. The ads featuring the players are utilized across national content and campaigns. So, yes, the fine that the NFL is trying to levy is thick with irony. But there is more because this could be perhaps the craziest NFL story of the year: Juszczyk's nickname is "Juice." When he makes a play for the 49ers at home, the crowd chants, "juuuuuuuuice." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! So, maybe, the guy wasn't pretending to chug a beer. Maybe the NFL, awash in beer sponsorships, assumed every time someone drinks, they are imbibing beer. Juszczyk told ESPN, "I don't even drink beer," and added on his social media, "Can't make this stuff up." The NFL also has an official juice agreement through Pepsico with Tropicana. But the league drink police didn't assume the guy nicknamed Juice was imitating taking a drink of juice. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Jacoby Brissett appears to slight another Cardinals wideout when talking about Marvin Harrison Jr.'s struggles
articles.summary: Michael Wilson got dragged into the Marvin Harrison Jr. drama.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals experienced a massive letdown during the team's Week 2 loss to the Seattle Seahawks . After taking down the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 1, there was hope the Cardinals could be better than anticipated. But getting beat 31-7 to any team — even the Super Bowl champs — can be humbling.

After a loss of that magnitude, it's not unusual for teams, media and/or fans to take a wider look at the team to figure out what went wrong. And the focal point of that criticism for the Cardinals has been wideout Marvin Harrison Jr.

Through two games, Harrison has one catch on four targets. That catch came in Week 1.

Quarterback Jacoby Brissett was asked about Harrison's numbers Wednesday. While Brissett was supportive and attempted to talk positively about Harrison, the quarterback may have unintentionally threw another one of his receivers under the bus.

During his defense of Harrison, Brissett pointed out that Michael Wilson — who just received a massive contract extension — caught just two balls against the Seahawks and wasn't being criticized for that.

It sounds … much worse than Brissett likely intended.

The quarterback was very likely trying to make the point that Harrison faces higher expectations and criticism compared to other players on the team and that's not fair. The entire offense — other than tight end Trey McBride — struggled, so why is Harrison getting the focus after the fact?

While Brissett's point isn't necessarily wrong, there are valid reasons Harrison faces higher expectations than most players on the team. When he was coming out of the draft with the No. 4 overall pick two years ago, Harrison — the son of Indianapolis Colts legend Marvin Harrison — was considered a "generational" talent. He was supposed to be a can't-miss prospect, one that would make an immediate impact before developing into a superstar.

After a modest rookie season, injuries and ineffectiveness prevented Harrison from putting up elite numbers during his second year in the NFL. Now, things appear to be going backward. The wideout's target share is an unacceptable number for a player who was supposed to be an undeniable star.

That's not to say Harrison will never reach his full potential. He shouldn't be written off as a finished product early in Year 3, especially after injuries halted his progress last season.

But — for both his sake and the Cardinals' sake — Harrison needs to start turning in better performances soon. It would, at the very least, quiet his doubters, and prevent Wilson from catching strays from his quarterback … even if that's not exactly what happened.

articles.title: Ravens' Anthony Weaver Jokes He'll Stop Calling QBs 'Poor Man' After Loss to Tyler Shough, Saints
articles.summary: Anthony Weaver has learned his lesson.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens defensive coordinator told reporters he would no longer refer to any quarterback as a "poor man's" version of a different quarterback after calling Tyler Shough a a "poor man's Josh Allen" before Sunday's showdown between the teams. Shough's controversial touchdown in the fourth quarter ultimately led New Orleans to a 24-17 win over the Ravens.

"I will just make sure I do not call any other quarterbacks 'poor man' because that is probably what propelled [Shough] essentially over the end zone," he joked with reporters.

In Weaver's defense, he was being complimentary of Shough in his original comments, saying the Saints' quarterback impressed him last season when New Orleans played the Miami Dolphins. Weaver was Miami's defensive coordinator last season.

"Has all the arm talent in the world [and] can run. I don't think he gets enough credit for how good [of] an athlete he is," Weaver told reporters last week. "... I just think the more reps he gets, the more confident he's going to get in that scheme and with the talent around him. I think they have done a good job of trying to build the talent around him. They have tremendous skill players. I think they have upgraded their offensive line from when I saw [them] a year ago. So, sky's the limit for the kid."

It was the "poor man" part of the comments that everybody latched onto, however. That included Saints' coaches, who started referring to Shough as "Poor Man" throughout the week.

"I loved it," Shough told reporters after Sunday's win. "I knew what [Weaver] meant by it, but yeah, obviously [Allen's] an elite player, but it fires me up."

The 26-year-old quarterback is making a name for himself this season, throwing for 662 yards, four touchdowns and two interceptions through two games while rushing for 31 yards and two touchdowns. He's led the Saints to a 1-1 record and the team was a failed two-point conversion in Week 1's overtime loss against the Detroit Lions away from stacking back-to-back wins to start the season.

Nobody is Allen. But the Saints are more than happy to have "Poor Man" on their side.

articles.title: Cowboys' Brian Schottenheimer Jokes He 'Thanked' NFL for 'Unique' Schedule Involving Brazil Game
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer says he thinks his team is prepared to navigate the unique challenge of playing three games, including one in Brazil, in a span of 12 days.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer says he thinks his team is prepared to navigate the unique challenge of playing three games, including one in Brazil, in a span of 12 days.

Schottenheimer has jokingly "thanked" the NFL for the schedule assignment, which starts with Sunday's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens in Brazil, per ESPN's Todd Archer .

The Cowboys are then set to travel for a road game against the Houston Texans the following Sunday, Oct. 4 before returning home for a Thursday, Oct. 8 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

"I'd be a hypocrite if I said I think it's a tough task, but we're up to it, and mentally tough we need to be," Schottenheimer told reporters Thursday. "This is a long season. I can't be a 'win-the-day' type of guy and be angry about it, but in reality, it's a long trip, come home, Houston, short week. But we're going to win today, and then we're going to go down there, and we're going to win Friday, Saturday, and play a really good team, and hopefully win that.

"It does require mental toughness, and the schedule is a schedule, and we will play anybody, anytime, anywhere. But it's a unique schedule for sure."

There's a two-hour time difference between Dallas and Rio de Janeiro, where Schottenheimer says the team has been planning the logistics of the trip since March.

Schottenheimer said during a Thursday appearance on 105.3 The Fan his plan was to compress preparation for the game into earlier in the week before flying to Brazil Thursday night for a short practice Friday and a visit to the stadium Saturday.

"Everything sounds like you wanna get down there at least 48 hours or so before the game, get a little bit adjusted, acclimated," Schottenheimer said.

The NFL season started off with an international matchup in Melbourne featuring two teams with radically different travel strategies in the San Francisco 49ers, who arrived early in Australia to adjust to the time difference, and the Los Angeles Rams, who conceded a blowout loss after attempting to keep their players on California time during the trip.

Sean McVay later called himself a "dumbass coach" for not giving his team more time to adjust to the travel.

The Cowboys and Ravens, in contrast, are both planning to fly to Brazil Thursday night and spend two days in the country ahead of the Week 3 matchup.

Both teams will hope giving players more time to adjust to international travel will help them prepare for Sunday's kickoff at 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Steelers' Joey Porter Jr. Calls Contract Talks 'Old News,' Updates Status amid Back Injury
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers and Joey Porter Jr. were unable to come to terms on a new contract ahead of the 2026 campaign, which means the cornerback has shifted his attention to recovering from a back injury.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers and Joey Porter Jr. were unable to come to terms on a new contract ahead of the 2026 campaign, which means the cornerback has shifted his attention to recovering from a back injury.

"It didn't get done," Porter told reporters when discussing the possibility of a new contract Thursday. "It didn't happen. That's really just old news for me now. It's mainly just focusing on what I have ahead of me and getting back to 100 percent."

He also said he "definitely" sees himself playing at some point this season before teammate DeShon Elliott voiced support when Porter was asked if there was any type of rift between him and the team:

Porter is playing on the final year of his deal and is being paid $3.9 million in base salary.

That alone would have made his contract status with the team a major storyline, but the failed negotiations also came during the same offseason the cornerback market was in the headlines with Devon Witherspoon and the Seattle Seahawks (four-year, $132 million) as well as Christian Gonzalez and the New England Patriots (four-year, $135 million) agreeing to new extensions.

As for Porter, Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette (h/t Ross McCorkle of Steelers Depot) reported the Steelers offered him a deal that would have paid him slightly more than $27 million in 2026.

However, Dulac previously reported the cornerback wanted at least $30 million a year in average annual salary.

There was no agreement in the offseason, and Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reported Pittsburgh had no plans on breaking its "longstanding organizational policy by resuming contract negotiations in-season."

Jonathan Jones of The Athletic reported "a trade is not out of the question on this stuff."

At this point, though, Porter didn't seem particularly interested in talking about his contract and instead discussed trying to recover from the back injury that kept him out of the first two games of the season.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Sunday the team was "planning" for him to take the field in Week 3 against the Cincinnati Bengals, although it depended on his conditioning level and how the back responded since it had "flared up when he's tried to go full speed."

The Steelers could certainly use him on the field, especially in a matchup against Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins with Cincinnati.

But his long-term future with the team will remain a topic until there is some type of resolution.

articles.title: Tom Brady 'Kind of Embarrassed' After Viral 'Piss Missile' Comment During Cowboys vs. Commanders
articles.summary: Tom Brady used some colorful language during the Fox broadcast of the Dallas Cowboys matchup against the Washington Commanders on Sunday, and he apologized to those who might have been offended by it on Thursday.
articles.body:
Tom Brady used some colorful language during the Fox broadcast of the Dallas Cowboys matchup against the Washington Commanders on Sunday, and he apologized to those who might have been offended by it on Thursday.

Brady, who described a pass from Dak Prescott as an "absolute piss missile," said he is "kind of embarrassed" by his comment. He also joked that the swear jar in his house is "getting way too full."

"I'm actually kind of embarrassed," Brady said. "There's a lot of grandmas at home that probably aren't very happy with my mouth on Fox. I'm gonna fix that. Sorry, I apologize."

In defense of Brady, calling Prescott's dime to CeeDee Lamb a "piss missile" might have been the best way to describe it. Still, it sounds like he's planning to use family-friendlier language next time he's in the booth.

Brady, who joined Fox on a 10-year, $375 million deal ahead of the 2024 season, will be on the call for Sunday's game between the Buffalo Bills and the Los Angeles Chargers.

articles.title: Malik Nabers Injured, Latest Updates on Giants WR After X-Rays on Shoulder Ahead of Titans Game
articles.summary: Monday's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams was just one of the New York Giants' concerns in Week 2, as quarterback Jaxson Dart (knee) and Malik Nabers (shoulder) suffered injuries.
articles.body:
Monday's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams was just one of the New York Giants' concerns in Week 2, as quarterback Jaxson Dart (knee) and Malik Nabers (shoulder) suffered injuries.

The latter returned, though. He provided an update to reporters on Thursday after getting X-rays.

He previously told reporters after the game he popped his shoulder back into place but would still get X-rays to see the extent of the damage.

"My shoulder's okay," Nabers said. "Gonna get an X-ray on it, see what's going on. I was out there, trying to just come back out. We had lost Jax, so I didn't want to give the team another loss."

The wide receiver missed time in the first half but returned to the contest and finished with one catch for one yard.

It was a far cry from Week 1 when Nabers tallied six catches for 69 yards in a victory over the division-rival Dallas Cowboys in his first game back since September 2025 due to a torn ACL that limited him to four games last season.

His health was a major focal point for the Giants coming into the season because of that 2025 setback, although Monday's injury was an upper-body one and not the knee.

When healthy, Nabers can be one of the best receivers in the league. After all, it wasn't long ago that he was a Pro Bowler as a rookie in 2024 with 109 catches for 1,204 yards and seven touchdowns.

He isn't the only concern for the Giants, as John Harbaugh announced on Wednesday that Dart will miss the rest of the regular season.

New York will likely rely on Jameis Winston with Dart out, and his job will be much easier if Nabers is available. If not, Darnell Mooney and Isaiah Likely will surely see more targets in the Giants' Week 3 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

articles.title: Giants' Cam Skattebo Reacts to Jaxson Dart's Season-Ending Knee Injury, 'My Best Friend'
articles.summary: The New York Giants have had a tough week after losing quarterback Jaxson Dart to a season-ending knee injury.
articles.body:
The New York Giants have had a tough week after losing quarterback Jaxson Dart to a season-ending knee injury.

Running back Cam Skattebo described Dart as his "best friend" and discussed the emotional impact of the injury.

"It's a little emotional for me. It sucked to lose him," Skattebo told reporters Thursday. "But we gotta move on. The team still has a full season left. Still got 15 games minimum left. It's something we have to battle through together as a team."

Schefter Talks Possible Giants QB Targets

During their Week 2 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, Dart took a hard hit to the legs and was ruled out of the game. It was later revealed that he would need season-ending surgery to repair his MCL, PCL and meniscus.

The Giants upset the Dallas Cowboys in Week 1 after Dart threw for 230 yards and three touchdowns, and that performance perhaps gave fans confidence that the 2026 campaign would be more than just a rebuilding year.

While New York's season is far from over, its playoff hopes took a big hit with Dart's season-ending injury.

articles.title: Madison Beer gets new skin while Justin Herbert sinks to 0-2, Aaron Rodgers' ex lashes out & NFL or college?
articles.summary: Madison Beer's new Fortnite video game skin debuts as her fiancé Justin Herbert and the Chargers prepare to face the Buffalo Bills on Sunday.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. Over the hump and safely onto the other side of the week. Our long, 72-hour nightmare without football is over. Thank goodness. Thursday night football tonight. College games tonight, tomorrow and Saturday. NFL back at it on Sunday. We've also got the Presidents Cup starting today, although nobody really cares about this one, and the final weekend of MLB regular season baseball. That's right. TEAM USA GOLFERS WELCOME TRUMP’S EXPECTED PRESIDENTS CUP VISIT, SHARE PRIDE IN REPRESENTING AMERICA The MLB playoffs start in less than a week. Red Sox-Yankees in the Bronx for a 3-game Wild Card series? How lucky are we? Best time of year, folks. Let's dig in. The trailer dropped today, and folks — it's a humdinger. I thought it was fake. It was not. OK, grab you a controller and some pizza rolls, and settle in for a Thursday 'Cap! So, we're gonna keep this class short and to the point, because A) there's football on in a few hours, and B) I have a new water pump to install so I can use the toilet without dumping a gallon of water in the back each time. Yep. I woke up this morning to the absolute worst noise of all time ... silence. I went to take my morning pee, flushed, started to walk away, and then stopped. I didn't hear anything. No refilling. No noise from the back. No slow leak that's been annoying me for a year now. Just silence. I went to fill up the coffee maker ... and nothing came out. The worst feeling in the world. I went outside, checked on the water tanks, and the silence was equally deafening. The pump, which started to fade back in May, had finally breathed its last breathe. So, our house has been water-less all day. I've got a new one en route as we speak. Until then, if it's yellow, let it mellow! OK, let's use some virtual water and cleanse ourselves with Madison Beer becoming a new video game character while Justin Herbert tries to simply get a win: What are our thoughts on the new Madden movie? Remember earlier this month when Aaron Rodgers called out most of his exes, including Danica Patrick? Well, another former lover — Milwaukee Bucks Heiress Mallory Edens — has decided to clap back: "My ex is currently on a press tour talking about how he never loved anyone he dated after 2017. Unfortunately for him, I am also on a press tour, for a movie inspired by how down bad I was. Really exciting time for competing narratives!!" Get him, Mal! Rodgers and Eden dated, briefly, back in 2022. It never really evolved into anything serious, but apparently, it left enough of a mark for Mallory to clap back at Aaron four years later. For those who missed it, here's what Rodgers said earlier this month: "No one cares what they have to say until they say my name. articles.title: 49ers' John Lynch Sidesteps Question on Mac Jones Trade Calls Amid QB Injuries Around NFL
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers general manager John Lynch didn't directly address a question regarding opposing teams calling about the availability of backup quarterback Mac Jones during a Thursday appearance on KNBR's "Murph & Markus."
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers general manager John Lynch didn't directly address a question regarding opposing teams calling about the availability of backup quarterback Mac Jones during a Thursday appearance on KNBR's "Murph & Markus."

"I got to leave that alone," Lynch said, via Tristi Rodriguez of NBC Sports Bay Area. "What I will tell you is, I think a lot of people see all that and say, OK, there's opportunity. It also tells you we're very fortunate to have a guy like Brock [Purdy], franchise quarterback, but then to have a guy like Mac in the event [of Purdy getting injured]. There's no more important position in football -- they're all important -- but I think we know as your quarterback goes, so goes your team. So, I think it's a really special situation to have Brock here and to have Mac here. And to have a guy we're really excited about with Kurtis Rourke.

"I think back to [former 49ers coach] Bill Walsh; maybe he was on to something when he had Joe Montana but he also brought Steve Young in here. It's a good position to be in a position of strength, and it provides opportunities in a number of ways, the most important way being that you're well insulated in the event something ever were to happen. And then there also are opportunities you receive calls and then you make decisions accordingly. But we love our situation at quarterback."

Several starting quarterbacks have already suffered injuries this season, including New York Giants passer Jaxson Dart , Washington Commanders signal-caller Jayden Daniels and Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams .

While the exact recovery timeline for Daniels and Williams is unknown, Dart is set to undergo season-ending surgery after suffering damage to his MCL, PCL and meniscus during a Week 2 matchup with the Los Angeles Rams.

Backup passer Jameis Winston is currently filling in under center, although Giants head coach John Harbaugh told reporters that the team is looking to make an external addition at quarterback on Wednesday.

ESPN's Adam Schefter also brought up Jones as a potential target for New York in a Thursday appearance on Get Up .

Purdy is off to a strong start to the 2026 season, helping the 49ers compile a 2-0 record.

He's completed 80.4 percent of his passes for 492 yards and five touchdowns compared to just one interception, averaging 8.8 yards per attempt. Purdy's 95.7 QBR ranks No. 1 among 32 qualified quarterbacks, via ESPN .

Even though his impressive play could cause San Francisco to consider parting ways with Jones, the 49ers may also choose to keep their backup in order to preserve their depth.

Purdy previously missed eight games during the 2025 season due to a toe injury , but the team was still able to make the playoffs with Jones filling in as his temporary replacement.

San Francisco went 5-3 in Jones' eight starts, as he threw for 2,151 yards and 13 touchdowns while getting picked off six times.

If Purdy gets hurt again and Jones is traded, the 49ers will need to rely on second-year passer Kurtis Rourke.

Rourke has showed promise in the preseason, but the 2025 seventh-round pick has yet to appear in a regular-season game.

As the 49ers look to go on a deep playoff run, they may choose to keep Jones despite potential trade interest in him.

articles.title: Frank Reich Says Analytics Played Role in 4th-and-1 Shotgun Run Play Call in Jets' Loss to Packers
articles.summary: New York Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich says analytics backed his decision to call a shotgun play rather than attempting to throw the ball on fourth-and-1 late in a tied Week 2 game last Sunday against the Green Bay Packers.
articles.body:
New York Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich says analytics backed his decision to call a shotgun play rather than attempting to throw the ball on fourth-and-1 late in a tied Week 2 game last Sunday against the Green Bay Packers.

Braelon Allen failed to run in the final yard to extend the Jets' final offensive drive of regulation. The Packers went on to win on an overtime field goal.

"I'm comfortable and confident in the calls that we called," Reich told reporters Thursday.

Reich said "context" for the decision to use the shotgun play included studies that showed teams, excluding quarterback sneaks, convert 71 percent of shotgun runs on fourth-and-1.

Teams recorded a 67 percent conversion rate when under center for the same play, Reich said.

"The reason it's better, percentage-wise over a five-year period, is because there's a threat of a pass, and they don't get so tight," Reich said. "So, we had that perspective going in."

Reich continued, "Unless you're an elite quarterback sneak team, and there's only three or four of those... if you're not one of those, the analytics would say a gun run, a gun direct run, is the best percentage call in that play."

He indicated he would have been more likely to attempt a sneak had the Jets been attempting to cover half a yard rather than a full yard on the fourth down.

Reich will get his next chance to put together clutch down conversions against a defense that has had one of the NFL's roughest starts to the 2026 season.

The Lions, which have allowed a league-worst 457 yards against per game through Week 2, are preparing to host the Jets this Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Nick Chubb Will Sign 1-Day Contract to Retire With Browns, RB Earned 4 NFL Pro Bowl Nods
articles.summary: Former NFL running back, four-time Pro Bowler and Cleveland Browns legend Nick Chubb will sign a one-day contract with his old team so he can officially retire as a Brown.
articles.body:
Former NFL running back, four-time Pro Bowler and Cleveland Browns legend Nick Chubb will sign a one-day contract with his old team so he can officially retire as a Brown.

James Wood "JW" Johnson III, managing partner of the Haslam Sports Group, made the announcement on Cleveland Browns Daily.

Underperforming Players With the Most to Prove 🏈

Chubb will sign the contract on Friday, when there will also be a retirement press conference. The Browns will also honor Chubb on Sunday, when the team will host its 2026 home opener against the Carolina Panthers.

The Browns selected Chubb, a former Georgia star, with the 35th overall pick in the 2018 NFL draft.

Chubb had authored an amazing comeback story in college after suffering a devastating left knee injury (dislocated kneecap, torn PCL, MCL and LCL) in 2015 . He rebounded with 2,591 yards from scrimmage and 24 touchdowns over the 2016 and 2017 seasons.

In the pros, Chubb immediately became the Browns' top running back and offensive weapon. He helped quickly turn around a team that went 0-16 the year before his arrival. Cleveland improved to 7-8-1 in Chubb's rookie season (2018) and made the playoffs for the first time in 18 years in 2020 after an 11-5 season.

The Browns also won their first playoff game since 1994, beating the AFC North champion Pittsburgh Steelers in the AFC Wild Card round.

Over his first five seasons, Chubb amassed 7,331 yards from scrimmage and 52 touchdowns. He had four 1,000-yard rushing seasons (2019-2022) and even made the All-Pro Second Team in 2022.

Chubb got off to a hot start in 2023, rushing for 170 yards on just 28 carries. Sadly, Chubb suffered a torn MCL and a damaged ACL in his left knee in Week 2 against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Chubb missed the rest of the 2023 season and the first six games of 2024. Unfortunately, Chubb's remarkably efficient form from his first six seasons (5.3 yards per carry) did not appear post-injury. He played one more season with Cleveland (2024) and a final campaign with the Houston Texans (2025). Thankfully, Chubb suited up for a near-full season in 2025 (15 games), amassing 573 yards and three scores.

For his career, Chubb finished with 8,458 yards from scrimmage and 59 touchdowns on 1,603 touches (5.3 yards per touch). He averaged 5.0 yards per carry.

There's no doubt Chubb was one of the NFL's best running backs of the past 10 years. Despite playing only five full seasons as an RB1, Chubb is ninth in the NFL in rushing yards since 2016.

Now he'll get his well-deserved love and respect from Cleveland faithful this week as Chubb officially retires as a Brown.

articles.title: 49ers' Kyle Juszczyk reportedly fined for beer-chugging celebration; Lions' Amon-Ra St. Brown fined four times for smoking gesture
articles.summary: Juszczyk has already said he is appealing the fine for his touchdown celebration against the Dolphins.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk and Indianapolis Colts guard Matt Goncalves have reportedly each been fined by the NFL for beer-chugging celebrations following Week 2 touchdowns, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

Both players received letters from the NFL this week regarding their fines with the league's message stating, "Your imitation of chugging a beer constituted an offensive demonstration and could reasonably be construed as being in poor taste."

Juszczyk, whose nickname is "Juice," caught a 6-yard touchdown pass in the third quarter of the 49ers' 35-13 win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. After celebrating with teammates, Juszczyk turned back towards the crowd while in the end zone and imitating chugging a drink.

The NFL, which has a deal with Anheuser-Busch InBev worth a reported $250 million per year, handed Juszczyk a fine of $14,926.

Juszczyk, who is appealing, sent a text to Schefter saying that he doesn't drink beer — a note that teammate George Kittle backed up in a X post saying , "Can confirm he doesn't really drink beer but is a good guy."

Kittle also decided to have some fun on social media with Juszczyk.

This is the second time this season that Juszczyk has been fined by the NFL. During Week 1, he was docked $20,033 for using his helmet while making a block during San Francisco 's win over the Los Angeles Rams in Australia.

Goncalves' wallet took a little less of a hit, according to Schefter. The Colts guard was docked only $8,847 for his beer-chugging celebration following Tyler Warren 's first quarter touchdown Sunday night against the Kansas City Chiefs .

After Warren's reception, he proceeded to imitate opening a can and handing it to Goncalves to chug before spiking the ball.

It's not known yet if Goncalves will join Juszczyk in filing an appeal.

As part of the appeal process, Juszczyk will have a hearing with one of the NFL's appeals officers — Derrick Brooks, Jordy Nelson or James Thrash — who are jointly appointed and paid by the league and the NFLPA. Once the officer makes a decision, the ruling is final and binding.

Bengals ' Ja'Marr Chase fined for elbow gesture after TD

Also receiving fines from the NFL for gestures during celebrations were Cincinnati Bengals receiver Ja'Marr Chase and Detroit Lions receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown .

Chase told reporters he was fined for emulating Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson's finishing move, "The People's Elbow" after a touchdown catch against the Houston Texans . And Chase's gesture was more for signaliing to the crowd that the move is coming, not the maneuver itself.

Perhaps the NFL misinterpreted the gesture and believed Chase was making a more obscene gesture. The bending of the elbow upwards does resemble one that means, to put it less rudely, "Up yours" but something typically more profane. The French would call it "Bras d'honneur." But Chase's chances of winning an appeal seem strong.

"I'm trying to figure out because that's not what it is," Chase told reporters, via OnSI . "This is literally like a wrestling move. You know what I'm saying? So I don't know. Maybe I should stop."

Amon-Ra St. Brown received four separate fines for apparent smoking gesture

St. Brown drew not one, but four separate fines for a celebration he performed during the Lions' matchup with the Buffalo Bills .

The gesture that compelled punishment from the NFL was apparently emulating smoking a joint, according to the Detroit News' Nolan Bianchi . St. Brown put his fingers to his mouth and mimicked inhaling four different times, once after a third-quarter touchdown catch and three other times after getting first downs.

St. Brown was fined for each of the gestures. At $14.000 per fine, he was docked a total of $56,000 for those celebratory gestures.

"It's not good, man. 14-something times four," the Lions receiver said to Bianchi. "You do the math."

St. Brown said he will appeal the fines. That one might not get much leniency from the league.

articles.title: Ohio State must prepare for Illinois QB Katin Houser | opinion
articles.summary: Illinois quarterback Katin Houser brings veteran savvy, accuracy and mobility into a difficult road test against the Buckeyes.
articles.body:
Perhaps no quarterback in the Big Ten Conference has the unusual resume of someone like Illinois quarterback Katin Houser . The fifth-year senior began his career at Michigan State , transferred to a lower level, and is now back in the Big Ten for his final season of college football.

Houser was a former four-star recruit from St. John Bosco High School in California who signed with Michigan State in 2022 and redshirted after playing just one game. The following season, he played in 11 games and made seven starts for the Spartans , completing 112-of-191 passes for 1,130 yards, six touchdowns, and five interceptions.

Houser left Michigan State after 2023 and found stability at East Carolina. He played in nine games in 2024 and started in seven of them. He passed for 2,006 yards and 18 touchdowns in his first season. The following season, Houser broke out to become one of the better quarterbacks in the country. He started all 12 regular-season games and threw for 3,300 yards and 19 touchdowns while completing 65.9% of his passes.

Houser signed with Illinois on Jan. 4, giving head coach Bret Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. the quarterback they wanted to replace the departing Luke Altmyer .

Through three games , Houser has been extremely efficient for the Illini. He has completed 74.1% of his passes, while throwing for over 250 yards per game. He has thrown eight touchdown passes so far this season, seven of them to wide receiver Collin Dixon.

For Ohio State , the central focus will be to get Houser out of rhythm and force him to improvise. He has proven that he does a great job going through his progressions and making the right decision more often than not. The Buckeyes will open up their Big Ten schedule on Saturday, and their first challenge will be up against one of the better quarterbacks in the conference.

articles.title: Bengals' Joe Flacco Reacts to Giants Trade Buzz on Video After Jaxson Dart's Season-Ending Injury
articles.summary: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart is out for the regular season after suffering a left knee injury, leading to speculation that Big Blue will add a quarterback to the roster even though Jameis Winston is now entrenched as the new starter.
articles.body:
New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart is out for the regular season after suffering a left knee injury, leading to speculation that Big Blue will add a quarterback to the roster even though Jameis Winston is now entrenched as the new starter.

Cincinnati Bengals backup quarterback Joe Flacco has been mentioned as a possibility , and Kelsey Conway of the Cincinnati Enquirer asked the 19-year veteran about the chatter on Thursday.

"I just get a kick out of it, I mean, because the stuff happened yesterday, but it's obviously not real and not true, but it was good enough to get people, like certain friends of mine, and things like that," Flacco began.

"It was good enough to get them to text me, 'Hey, I'll see you in New York.' And I was like, 'No guys, you won't, you know that's not true.'

"I kind of just get a little kick out of it, I haven't really given it too much thought at this point.

Conway also asked Flacco how he manages his desire to play with the fact that he's happy with his current home in Cincinnati.

"In these cases, it's not up to me," Flacco said. "I'm on the Cincinnati Bengals and because of that, that's my focus. Being here, doing the things that I need to do to get better each day while I'm here. Make sure I'm absorbing the game plan and all of those things. I get a little bit of a kick out of it, but it's kind out of my hands. I'm a Cincinnati Bengal, and I'm doing everything I can to get ready for the Pittsburgh Steelers."

As Conway noted, it doesn't make sense for the Bengals to part ways with Flacco.

"It's highly unlikely the Bengals would be interested in trading Flacco. Cincinnati gave Flacco a lucrative deal for a backup position because of how much they value him. Flacco's contract is $6 million for one season and can go up to $9 million with incentives.

"For the Bengals to shell out that much money for a player who doesn't even start, it shows how highly the organization thinks of him. The Bengals saw the importance of having a backup quarterback who can carry the offense and win games in 2025."

As for the Giants, they just signed Winston to a two-year, $13.5 million contract extension. Simply put, Big Blue paid a premium for a high-end backup quarterback in case Dart was lost to injury. Sadly, that's the case, so now Winston is calling the shots.

One can surmise the talk about the Giants bringing in a quarterback has popped up because Winston played poorly in relief of Dart in a 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams last Monday.

Winston completed just 11-of-27 passes for 111 yards, no touchdowns and one interception. Those are concerning numbers any way one slices it.

However, Winston kept the Giants competitive in two starts in relief of Dart last year, completing 37-of-65 passes for 567 yards and two touchdowns (two picks) while rushing for 23 yards and one score. He also caught a 33-yard touchdown on a trick play.

Both games ended in losses (27-20 to the Green Bay Packers and 34-27 in overtime to the Detroit Lions), but the Giants were in both games.

New York has a pair of winnable home games coming up against the Tennessee Titans and Arizona Cardinals. If Winston plays well, he'll quiet any quarterback talk. If he doesn't, the speculation will only grow that New York will look elsewhere in order to salvage the season. Before that stretch, ESPN's Adam Schefter has already connected the Giants to San Francisco 49ers backup Mac Jones and Arizona Cardinals second-stringer Gardner Minshew.

For now, though, Winston is QB1, and he'll lead the Giants out of the tunnel against Tennessee on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Why Bengals believe leaning less on Joe Burrow gives them a chance to do more
articles.summary: The Bengals don't want Burrow to feel like he has to be Superman every week, as he has in years past. That's why an improved defense changes everything.
articles.body:
From the podium after the Bengals ' 20-6 win over the Texans , Joe Burrow assessed his performance.

"I was incredibly average today," Burrow said Sunday. "We're going to keep getting better. It was a great win. We did some good things, but a lot to learn from."

Burrow's pair of deep-ball touchdowns to Ja'Marr Chase in Houston were hardly average. And yet, the three-time Pro Bowl quarterback's evaluation of his day at large reflected more than just a quarterback being hard on himself.

The Bengals don't aspire for their quarterback to be "average," per se. And there are pieces around him that need to step up, such as the offensive line allowing Burrow to face blitzes on 37% of dropbacks through two weeks, the highest rate of his career, per Next Gen Stats.

But also: the Bengals don't want Burrow to look like Superman every week, as he has in some years past.

More precise: They don't want him to need to.

"You talk about when are the appropriate times to have that dial turned toward 'I have to be a playmaker' versus one of the times to have that dial turned forward, 'I have to mange this football game and keep myself upright,'" Bengals offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher told Yahoo Sports during training camp. "That's a discussion I think you always have to have. And for great, talented players, they have to think about that a lot."

Pitcher said that Burrow, whose offense has outperformed its defensive counterpart throughout his Bengals career, thinks about that often.

"The goal would be that we create a team, all three phases, that allows us to be in fewer situations where [Burrow] feels like, 'I have to go make this play come hell or high water.'"

Two games is hardly a representative sample size. But through two games, the Bengals' defense has provided Burrow with more reason to believe than they have in at least four campaigns.

After ranking 31st of 32 in yardage allowed last season and 30th in points allowed, Cincinnati ranks 16th in yards allowed and eighth in scoring defense through two weeks.

The Bengals traded the 10th overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft for defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II in April. They also collected key offseason acquisitions, including safety Bryan Cook , outside linebacker Boye Mafe and defensive tackle Jonathan Allen .

The group is changing the Bengals' defensive reputation week by week — and changing how Burrow considers in-game scenarios.

"You just play a little more conservative," Burrow said after the Texans game. "Those guys have been great. When you have that rush and that coverage, you try not to mess it up."

Burrow fantasy owners may regret that the quarterback who led the NFL two years ago (his last fully healthy season) by passing for 4,918 yards and 43 touchdowns may not actually be chasing similar numbers.

But the Bengals believe this formula gives them a better chance at contending for the Super Bowl as it returns to Los Angeles ' SoFi Stadium, home of the Bengals' last big-stage appearance. They believe alleviating Burrow's burden increases the chances he finishes the season healthy, as he enters this year having missed at least six games in three of his six prior seasons.

"Throwing for all these yards and scoring all these points, sure, that's good," Pitcher said. "But unless we're playing for division championships and playoff seeds, and playing in January and February, that's the only thing that really matters now.

"I really feel that from Joe and some of the other guys as well."

Burrow on Lawrence: 'Dex really set the tone'

To improve from a bottom-three defense, the bar is low.

To maintain it for two weeks could prove to be a mirage at season's end.

But the Bengals don't expect their new-look defense to falter.

Perhaps the Texans won't rebound to a strong offensive year. But the Bengals held Houston to 6 points one week after the Buffalo Bills allowed Houston 31. The Bengals limited the Texans to a 29.41% third-down success rate and reduced QB C.J. Stroud 's completion percentage 14 points from a week prior.

The absence of receiver Nico Collins (hamstring) likely explains some of the divergence, Collins accounting for 75 yards and a touchdown against the Bills. But does that fully account for the Texans dropping from 4-of-5 in the red zone to 0-of-4?

The Texans did not reach the end zone at all, breaking the Bengals' 65-game streak allowing touchdowns. (The Bills now hold that record at 47 games, per Next Gen Stats, after the Bengals kept an opponent from scoring a touchdown for the first time since Week 3 of the 2022 NFL season).

The Bengals seemed at risk of allowing another score halfway through the second quarter on Sunday, when Stroud hit running back David Montgomery for 8 yards on third-and-9. All Houston needed was inches to convert the first down from the Bengals' 17-yard line, a chance to score in a scoreless game.

Lawrence had other plans. He slipped through his block quickly, finding Montgomery in the backfield for the loss of a yard. Turnover on downs. Bengals ball.

"Dex really set the tone on that first fourth-and-1, getting that big stop … " Burrow said. "He set the tone for the rest of the day."

Burrow marched down the field with passes of 18 and 23 yards to Tee Higgins , before delivering a 32-yard pass to Ja'Marr Chase in the front right corner of the end zone. An acrobatic Chase eluded Texans All-Pro cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. , dragging his feet in the end zone as he spun before falling out of bounds.

Burrow escaped the pocket in the third quarter to again find Chase, this time on an 18-yard touchdown threaded between defenders.

The highlights looked as good as ever, but with 10 failed third-down conversions and two drives stalling in favor of a field goal, the Bengals also had dry spells. That didn't keep them from pressing after their defense allowed 28.9 points per game last season.

A year after ranking dead-last by allowing 147.1 rushing yards per game, the Bengals currently rank third, allowing 74.5.

Lawrence has proven a key factor there, the Bengals limiting the Texans to 1 rushing yard per carry on 12 run snaps with Lawrence in the game compared to 8 yards per carry on the six without him, per Next Gen Stats.

And he's far from the only Bengals defender making plays. Teammates Jonathan Allen, Cedric Johnson (twice) and Shemar Stewart each sacked Stroud. Cornerback Dax Hill, safety Jordan Battle , cornerback DJ Turner II and nickel Jalen Davis deflected passes. Linebacker Barrett Carter , Allen, Johnson and Stewart joined Lawrence in registering tackles for loss. And six defenders posted quarterback hits.

"They've lived up to the hype through [two] weeks," Burrow told reporters Wednesday. "But just as we've talked about at our games and in here — it's two weeks. We're still in September. We're not even close to where we want to be, nor is anybody.

"2-0 isn't gonna get anything done in this league. Got to keep going."

What 0-2 history teaches Burrow about 2-0

The need to keep momentum going was evident at the Bengals' Aug. 3 training camp practice, as Cincinnati's defense outplayed its offense in a sign that this year might be different.

From Lawrence through the defensive backs, an energy simmered.

"Honestly, he's been terrorizing practice," Chase told Yahoo Sports from his locker afterward. "They terrorizing practice. DBs playing with confidence behind. …

"It definitely gives us confidence to see."

Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers , whom the Bengals will face on the road this Sunday, used the same buzzword to describe what he sees on film.

"They're playing with a lot of confidence," Rodgers said, "and it will be a good test for us."

The Steelers' offense has looked far from confident, coming off a 20-3 loss to the Patriots in which Rodgers was pressured on 38.6% of his dropbacks, the second-highest rate since he joined the Steelers last season, per Next Gen Stats.

The 3 points tied the second-fewest of Rodgers' 259 career starts, per Next Gen Stats.

The Bengals travel to Pittsburgh as 3.5-point road favorites for their first divisional matchup.

At stake: Cincinnati's first 3-0 start since 2015.

Burrow knows the Steelers' defense won't be shy at pressuring him nor batting his passes, describing T.J. Watt 's pick 6 vs. Atlanta in Week 1 as "crazy" but "certainly not lucky." The Steelers claim responsibility for a league-high 10 of Burrow's 52 career interceptions, the Steelers also forcing five Burrow fumbles (three lost) across 11 games.

So while the defensive makeover should reassure the Steelers of a more evenly distributed load, and more cushion for games in which Burrow feels he played "incredibly average," Burrow cautions against overconfidence because of a 2-0 start.

"We've been 0-2 before and rattled off 10 in a row," he said. "We can do the same the other way. So, we just got to keep going."

articles.title: NFL Insider Lists Justin Fields Among Giants QB Trade Targets to Replace Injured Jaxson Dart
articles.summary: The New York Giants are going to be without young quarterback Jaxson Dart for the remainder of the season, meaning Jameis Winston is currently in line to operate as the starter.
articles.body:
The New York Giants are going to be without young quarterback Jaxson Dart for the remainder of the season, meaning Jameis Winston is currently in line to operate as the starter.

But the Giants could seek another option in free agency or via a trade. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport speculated on Thursday that veteran free agent Jimmy Garoppolo is the "top option" among unsigned players and such a move is a "possibility if [Winston] does not play well."

As for trades, he listed a trio of backups—Arizona's Gardner Minshew II, Kansas City's Justin Fields and Pittsburgh's Mason Rudolph—as "some of the names to keep an eye on."

Stylistically, Fields might be the closest fit to the dual threat Dart provided when healthy, though the Chiefs would have to also be willing to trade their backup quarterback. That doesn't seem terribly likely just one season removed from Patrick Mahomes suffering a torn ACL, though if the Chiefs brought in a different backup it could be feasible.

Kansas City does have Garrett Nussmeier on the roster but he's an unproven rookie.

The Cardinals and Steelers may make more sense as potential trade partners. Arizona also has rookie Carson Beck on the roster and may be more inclined to give a rookie a long evaluation period than a Chiefs team with Super Bowl aspirations. And the Steelers kept four quarterbacks on the roster, with both Will Howard and Drew Allar waiting in the wings.

Still, the most likely scenario is a Garoppolo signing if Winston struggles. The 34-year-old spent the 2024-25 seasons serving as Matt Stafford's backup in Los Angeles and made one start in that time, throwing for 334 yards, two touchdowns and an interception in a Week 18 loss in the 2024 campaign.

The hope in New York, obviously, is that Winston will play far better than Monday's dreadful performance against the Rams (11-for-27 with 111 yards, no touchdowns, one interception and two sacks taken). Working full-time with the starters in practice should help in that regard.

But if Winston falters, the Giants are going to have to carefully consider their options as they look to salvage a once-promising 2025 season.

articles.title: Puka Nacua Likely Out for Rams vs. Broncos With Injury, Top Waiver-Wire WR Replacements for Fantasy
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is "unlikely to play" on Sunday evening at the Denver Broncos as he continues to deal with hip and groin concerns, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is "unlikely to play" on Sunday evening at the Denver Broncos as he continues to deal with hip and groin concerns, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

As noted by ESPN's Sarah Barshop , Nacua is listed with a hip ailment on the Rams' injury report. Head coach Sean McVay told reporters the wideout is also dealing with "a little bit of soreness" in his groin. He missed his second straight practice on Thursday.

So it appears Nacua will now miss his second straight game after sitting the Rams' 28-6 home win over the New York Giants in Week 2.

From a fantasy perspective, here's a look at five wide receivers to consider if players need a starter in Nacua's place. All players listed here are available in 51 percent or more in Yahoo leagues.

Baltimore Ravens WR Rashod Bateman (Available in 68% of Leagues)

Miami Dolphins WR Malik Washington (84%)

With Zay Flowers ( hamstring ) sidelined last week, Baltimore Ravens wideout Rashod Bateman caught seven passes for 88 yards and a touchdown on nine targets in a 24-17 home loss to the New Orleans Saints.

Flowers hasn't practiced this week, putting his availability in doubt for the Ravens' matchup with the Dallas Cowboys in Brazil on Sunday.

Only two players had more than three targets last Sunday: Bateman and tight end Mark Andrews (seven). The guess here is quarterback Lamar Jackson looks Bateman's way frequently again.

Like the Ravens, the Houston Texans lost their No. 1 wide receiver (Nico Collins) to a hamstring injury in Week 2. Collins hasn't practiced in Week 3, leaving his status in doubt for Sunday at the Indianapolis Colts.

Texans' playmakers had chances to step up last Sunday against the Cincinnati Bengals, but the offense struggled in a 20-6 defeat.

This Sunday brings more chances for success against a Colts team that's allowed 74 points in two weeks. That means wide receiver Keyshon Boutte could get his time to shine. Boutte had a quiet game Sunday (three catches, 37 yards), but he played a healthy 72 percent of the snaps and could certainly break out here.

This is a spot where it's hard to ignore the production. Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver Tre Tucker broke out for 119 yards and a touchdown on five catches (seven targets) in a 26-14 road win over the Los Angeles Chargers last Sunday. Clearly, he has found a good rapport with veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins.

Granted, the Raiders' top pass-catcher (tight end Brock Bowers) was out with a knee ailment. He may be back Sunday at the New Orleans Saints after logging a pair of practices this week.

Still, Tucker is clearly the Raiders' top wideout right now, so he'll get his looks. And the Raiders' offense did well thanks in large part to his efforts, so one can surmise the team should go back to that well Sunday.

The Miami Dolphins are banged up at wideout heading into a matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs. Caleb Douglas has missed both practices this week, and Chris Bell suited up for both, albeit in limited fashion.

This may be a spot for Malik Washington to rise. Washington leads the team in targets with 13 through two weeks, though it hasn't translated into much production (seven catches, 96 yards). Still, Washington will have opportunities, maybe even more now that Douglas is potentially out.

Chicago Bears wide receiver Kalif Raymond leads the team in receptions (13), receiving yards (124) and targets (14), and that would have been near-impossible to predict before the season given a roster including tight end Colston Loveland and wideouts Rome Odunze and Luther Burden. Alas, he's the top producer right now.

It's unclear how long that will last, but it's at least worth considering riding the lightning right now and hoping Raymond stays hot.

There is a big question at quarterback, of course, with starter Caleb Williams (hamstring) and backup Tyson Bagent (concussion protocol) not practicing this week , leaving third-stringer (but capable veteran) Case Keenum as the possible starter. However, Raymond is getting his fair share of opportunities, and that could very well continue Monday.

articles.title: NFL insider views Patriots as trade fit for WR Marvin Harrison Jr.
articles.summary: NFL insider Albert Breer was asked if the Patriots should consider trading for Cardinals receiver Marvin Harrison Jr.
articles.body:
Heading into the 2024 NFL Draft, some wondered if the New England Patriots should have selected Ohio State wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. over North Carolina's Drake Maye .

The Patriots needed Maye more, but there was a running argument that the team would be better off filling other positions on offense to create a better situation overall for a young quarterback. Ultimately, the team made the right decision and drafted the quarterback.

However, they might now be in a position to land both, two years after that fateful draft night.

Maye, who was the runner-up for MVP and led the Patriots to the Super Bowl in 2025, looks the part of an elite franchise quarterback. Harrison, on the other hand, has struggled to live up to the otherworldly hype that he had coming out of college.

It has led to swirling trade rumors about the former Buckeye. With A.J. Brown on injured reserve with a high ankle sprain, NFL insider Albert Breer was asked if the Patriots should show interest in the former first-round draft pick.

Breer seemed to like the idea, pointing to Mike Vrabel's tough coaching style as a fit to potentially get the best out of Harrison.

"I had a chance to kind of dig into [the problems with Harrison] with a few people who have coached him, a few people who are coaching him. What kept coming up was a toughness issue. ...To be a bigger receiver in the NFL you have to be really rugged," Breer said on Zolak & Bertrand . "Being big and being rugged aren't the same things. If you're a bigger player, it probably means you aren't separating in the same way a smaller guy is. ...So who can get through to him on the toughness part of it?

"Mike Vrabel would probably be one of the guys who could. It's something that I would probably consider because I think if they're willing to give him up for like a Day 3 pick and you're talking about, A.J. Brown, you want him to be your No. 1 when he comes back and then maybe he's your No. 1 for another year, but then you don't have an answer beyond that. That's where it might be worth taking the flyer."

A Day 3 pick would be a tempting trade offer for a player with untapped elite potential.

Of course, the Cardinals would have to be willing to make that deal, which would be a shocking discount for the No. 4 overall pick in 2024. It's important to note that Brown is expected to return at some point this season, and the team also invested heavily in Romeo Doubs in free agency.

Those two moves are part of the reason why they decided to trade Kayshon Boutte to the Houston Texans . With that said, Harrison was viewed as a generational talent entering the NFL draft. Even if the Patriots are set at receiver, they'd have to take a move of that magnitude under consideration, at the very least.

Follow Patriots Wire on Twitter and Facebook .

articles.title: Joe Flacco responds to Giants trade rumors: Bengals QB says it’s “not true”
articles.summary: The Bengals have one of the best quarterback situations in the NFL, but chatter about their backup has popped up.
articles.body:
There was a brief bit of Joe Flacco -to-New York chatter on Thursday after Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered an injury, but don't expect the Bengals quarterback to start packing his bags for the Big Apple just yet.

Flacco addressed the trade speculation in an interview with Kelsey Conway of The Cincinnati Enquirer , making it pretty clear that he has no reason to believe Cincinnati is looking to move him.

"I have no reason to believe that," Flacco said when asked if he expects to be traded.

The veteran quarterback even said some of his friends had already started joking with him about a potential reunion with Giants head coach John Harbaugh, who coached Flacco in Baltimore .

"It's obviously not real and not true, but it was good enough to get people, certain friends of mine, to text me, 'Hey I'll see you in New York,'" Flacco said. "I was like, 'No, guys, you won't, that's not true.'"

Of course, Flacco also knows better than most that things can change quickly in the NFL.

He didn't exactly see his move to Cincinnati coming last season, either. The Browns traded Flacco to the Bengals after Joe Burrow 's season-ending injury, putting the veteran in position to start four games for Cincinnati.

"I had no idea I was going to get traded last year, so you never know," Flacco said.

That may be the most important caveat here.

Flacco is currently the Bengals' backup to Burrow, and he's made it clear that he remains focused on Cincinnati. But if another quarterback-needy team comes calling, the Bengals will ultimately have the decision to make.

For now, though, Flacco isn't expecting anything to happen.

"I'm a Cincinnati Bengal, and I'm doing everything I can to get ready for the Pittsburgh Steelers ," he said.

And given what happened to him last year, he probably won't be taking anything for granted.

articles.title: Chiefs' Chris Jones to Give NIL Money to Keep Heisman Candidate Kamario Taylor at Mississippi State
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs star defensive tackle Chris Jones revealed that he plans to donate to Mississippi State's NIL fund in order to help keep Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor at the school beyond the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs star defensive tackle Chris Jones revealed that he plans to donate to Mississippi State's NIL fund in order to help keep Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor at the school beyond the 2026 season.

"I'm going to donate some (NIL), though, we've got to keep this quarterback — we've got to keep him around," Jones told reporters Thursday (h/t Alex Byington of On3.com). "With all these NIL teams spending $45 to $50 million a year, the salary cap doesn't exist in college, so definitely trying to keep our quarterback with us."

Before Jones became a seven-time Pro Bowler and three-time Super Bowl champion with the Chiefs, he spent three seasons at Mississippi State from 2013-15.

The Bulldogs have opened their 2026 campaign with a 3-0 record, sitting at No. 24 in the latest AP Top 25 poll . They've been successful largely due to the efforts of Taylor, who has thrived to begin his sophomore season.

In three games, he's completed 68.3 percent of his throws for 832 yards and 11 touchdowns compared to just one interception. Taylor has also made plays with his legs, rushing for 178 yards and one score.

The 19-year-old's hot start has already put him in the Heisman Trophy race .

If Taylor can put together an impressive overall season, it isn't hard to imagine several schools attempting to land him as a transfer at the end of the year.

Mississippi State athletic director Zac Selmon confirmed that the school will push to keep the signal-caller, though.

"We're going to be as competitive as we need to be," Selmon told On3.com's Andy Staples .

It appears as though Jones will also help contribute to the Bulldogs' efforts.
